01 · StructureJPK
tensioncompression
The real one, from below

The cantilever truss

Each truss reaches out over the seating with no column at the tip. So it must carry everything back to one support.

Under wind uplift, what happens to the bottom chord?
Stress reversal. A light membrane roof can be lifted by wind more than it is pushed down by its own weight. Members (and especially their connections) must be checked both ways. Repeated load cycling is why connection design and inspection get so much attention. Toggle Wind uplift above to see it.

02 · SkinJPK
One panel: lifted in one direction, pulled down in the other = anticlastic (saddle)
From below: arc beams lift the fabric, edges pull it down

Tension-only fabric

No bending stiffness, no compression. Its stiffness comes from shape + prestress, not thickness.

The membrane materialGlass-fibre fabric coated with PTFE (the "non-stick" coating), joined by heat-welded seams: no stitching

Why can't a membrane roof panel be flat?
A flat sheet resists load only by sagging. Opposite curvatures let one fibre direction take downward load and the other uplift. The shape is found by computer, not drawn.

03 · WaterJPK
Section through a valley gutter between two membrane panels (schematic)

Designing for water

Every square metre of fabric sends its rain to a few metres of gutter. Getting that water away fast is a structural decision as much as a plumbing one.

How would you design a gutter that's easy to maintain?
Design for the whole life, not just day one: falls so water never sits, outlets sized for tropical storms, access for cleaning, and steel that can be seen, reached and recoated. Kuching gets heavy downpours almost daily in the wet season.

Pick a steel layer to highlight it

04 · UpgradeJPK
Upgrade works in progress around the main grandstand

Upgrading an existing roof

New-build design starts from a blank page. An upgrade starts from what is really there.

We have the original drawings. Why survey at all?
Drawings record what was designed. Years of sun, rain and modifications mean the engineer must verify what was built and how it is today. Every upgrade design is checked against measured, on-site information.

Applying primer to horizontal surfaces, levels 1 & 2
Concrete terrace· cleaned and roughened
Primer + sand· for grip
Waterproof layer· about 2 mm, sprayed on
Anti-slip layer· safe for spectators
Sun-protection topcoat· keeps its colour

Typical terrace joint (riser/tread). The membrane dips into the joint instead of being stretched tight across it, so it can open and close without tearing.

Polyurea gels in seconds. Good news or bad news?
Both. People can walk on it within an hour and rain can't wash it off, but there's no time to fix mistakes. So all the checks happen before spraying.
